details:
AstroFlame AI — Project Details

AstroFlame AI is a research exploration platform designed to make NASA's microgravity combustion research easier to understand and investigate. Developed for NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026's "Flame in Freefall" challenge, it uses data from NASA's Physical Sciences Informatics (PSI-26) Burning and Suppression of Solids (BASS) investigation.

What does AstroFlame AI do, and how does it work?

AstroFlame AI organizes NASA's research datasets into three interactive sections:

  • ISS BASS Combustion Explorer: Allows users to filter experimental records by fuel-material category and sample geometry, examine dataset summaries, and explore visualizations.
  • BASS Configuration Explorer: Lets users select fuel and sample descriptions to investigate planned test points, sample identifiers, and experimental configurations.
  • Scientific Methodology: Explains the scientific background, NASA data sources, and limitations of the information being explored.

Together, these features make it easier to navigate complex research records without requiring users to manually interpret large spreadsheets.

What benefits does AstroFlame AI provide?

AstroFlame AI improves the accessibility and organization of NASA's combustion research data. Instead of navigating separate spreadsheets, users can interact with filters, charts, summaries, and configuration tables in one place. The platform also encourages responsible scientific interpretation by distinguishing planned experimental configurations from measured results.

What is the intended impact?

Fire safety is an important consideration for long-duration space missions. In microgravity, buoyancy-driven airflow is greatly reduced, changing how heat, oxygen, and combustion products move around flames.

AstroFlame AI aims to make research about these phenomena easier to explore, helping students, educators, and interested researchers engage with NASA's experimental work.

In the future, the platform could be expanded to incorporate additional measured experimental outcomes and support more advanced, scientifically validated analysis.

What tools and technologies were used?

  • Python: Core application logic and data processing.
  • Streamlit: Interactive web application and dashboard interface.
  • Pandas: Loading, cleaning, filtering, and organizing NASA datasets.
  • Plotly: Interactive data visualizations.
  • CSV datasets: NASA PSI-26 BASS experimental records and planned test matrix.
  • GitHub: Source-code management and project repository.
  • Streamlit Community Cloud: Application deployment and hosting.

How is AstroFlame AI creative?

AstroFlame AI transforms scientific research tables into an interactive exploration experience. Rather than simply displaying raw data, it combines filtering, visual summaries, configuration exploration, and scientific explanations in a single platform.

Its three-section structure connects experimental data, planned research configurations, and the scientific context behind the investigation.

What factors did the team consider?

The development process considered:

  • Scientific accuracy: Avoiding conclusions that the available datasets cannot support.
  • Data interpretation: Distinguishing experimental records from planned test configurations.
  • Usability: Making complex research information easier to navigate.
  • Transparency: Identifying NASA sources and explaining dataset limitations.
  • Expandability: Designing the platform so additional experimental measurements and analysis capabilities could be incorporated in the future.

How was Super Intelligence (AI) used?

ChatGPT (OpenAI) was used as an AI-assisted research and development tool throughout the creation and preparation of AstroFlame AI.

It assisted with:

  • Research and data interpretation: Helping understand NASA's PSI-26 BASS datasets, their structure, and the scientific context of combustion in microgravity.
  • Ideation and brainstorming: Discussing possible approaches and organizing the application's features.
  • Coding and debugging: Providing Python and Streamlit coding guidance, suggesting code changes, and helping troubleshoot application errors.
  • Writing and documentation: Helping draft and refine project descriptions, dataset explanations, and documentation.
  • Presentation preparation: Helping organize the presentation and prepare submission materials.

ChatGPT was used as an assistant during development and preparation. It is not integrated into the application as a predictive model or an AI-powered fire-safety system.
